blocks.text: Central Abbotsford homes listed and sold, June to October 2026

Central Abbotsford, October 2026. Detached houses: 79 listed at month end and 6 sold in October, a sales ratio of 8% (a buyers’ market). Condos and townhomes: 236 listed at month end and 42 sold in October, a sales ratio of 18% (a balanced market).

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 33 sold over 5 months against an average of 74.0 listed, about 11.2 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was September with 12 sold. Condos and townhomes: 209 sold over 5 months against an average of 262.6 listed, about 6.3 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 51 sold.

At street level, Central Abbotsford is the Bevan Avenue school corridor and the streets around Mill Lake and South Fraser Way.
People call this ground both Central Abbotsford and Downtown Abbotsford, and also name it by Mill Lake and Sevenoaks.
Matsqui Recreation Centre at 3106 Clearbrook Road sits at the west edge of the central area.
Detached streets here include infill lots created under the RS7 zone. RS7 allows new interior lots down to 300 m², smaller than the RS3 minimum of 540 m² and the RS5 minimum of 420 m².
The RS3-i (Urban Residential Zone, Infill) zone is named in City council material for Maple Street in the Historic Downtown plan area.
Detached homes are freehold, while condos and townhomes are strata under the Strata Property Act.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The neighbourhood angle on the city-wide rules is infill: check the lot's exact zone before valuing suite or multi-unit potential.
In the Historic Downtown plan area, the Urban 3 – Infill designation covers single detached dwellings with some ground-oriented duplexes.
Abbotsforward 2050 directs a Primary Transit Corridor along South Fraser Way between Clearbrook and McCallum Road, which affects lots fronting that corridor.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Abbotsford Middle and Abbotsford Senior Secondary sit on the same Bevan Avenue corridor as Godson and Dormick Park elementaries. Godson is at 33130 Bevan Avenue and Abbotsford Senior Secondary at 33355 Bevan Avenue.
The Abbotsford library branch shares the 33355 Bevan Avenue address with Abbotsford Senior Secondary.
Sevenoaks Shopping Centre on South Fraser Way is named in the City study as the City Centre's major retail centre, with West Oaks Mall and Clearbrook Town Square also named as City Centre malls.
Willband Creek runs through the Historic Downtown and central area, so creek-adjacent lots need a parcel check even away from any floodplain name.
Bourquin Exchange, the city's central bus exchange, sits inside this neighbourhood's street pattern.

The neighbourhood-specific point is billing district: homes in the Clearbrook Waterworks District are billed quarterly for sewer, while other Abbotsford water and sewer customers are billed bi-monthly.
Route 5 (Clearbrook/Bourquin via Hospital) links this neighbourhood directly to the hospital area.
Routes 1, 2, 4, 12, 17 and 31 (Abbotsford/Mission) are named in BC Transit service material for Abbotsford, with Bourquin Exchange as the central timing point.
South Fraser Way is the commercial backbone street, with George Ferguson Way, McCallum Road, Clearbrook Road, Ware Street and Old Yale Road as the other main roads named in City plan material.

blocks.text: Central Abbotsford: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check Willband Creek setbacks and floodplain status for the specific lot in the City WebMap before removing subjects.
Check the Historic Downtown designation for the lot before planning an exterior rebuild, because the plan sets expected form street by street.

faq.a: Godson and Dormick Park are among the feeder schools. Abbotsford Middle states feeder students living in its catchment are automatically registered for September, and its family groups with Abbotsford Senior Secondary, so the Bevan corridor chain is consistent across both test addresses run.
faq.q: Which elementary schools feed Abbotsford Middle here?

faq.a: New RS7 interior lots can go down to 300 m². City material states a 10.0 m minimum width and 22.5 m minimum depth for RS7, which is materially smaller than older RS3 lots, so frontage and depth must both be measured on the specific lot.
faq.q: How small can an infill lot be on these streets?

faq.a: Mill Lake Park is the central green space, with access from Bevan Avenue and Emerson Street. Centennial Outdoor Pool at 2310 Emerson Street sits in the Mill Lake area, and Matsqui Recreation Centre at 3106 Clearbrook Road serves the west edge.
faq.q: Is Mill Lake the recreation centre of this neighbourhood?

faq.a: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre is at 32900 Marshall Road, east of the central area. The closer walk-in option inside the area is the Abbotsford Urgent and Primary Care Centre at Unit 100, 2692 Clearbrook Road.
faq.q: Where is the hospital from these streets?

faq.a: Enter the primary home address into the SD34 School Locator portal; SD34 school pages state the portal determines the neighbourhood catchment school, and registration starts at the catchment school. Locator runs for two central test addresses: 33130 Bevan Ave returns Godson Elementary → Abbotsford Middle → Abbotsford Senior Secondary, and 32161 Dormick Avenue returns Dormick Park Elementary → Abbotsford Middle → Abbotsford Senior Secondary (SD34 School Locator, mybaragar.com, run 2026-11-01).
faq.q: How are school catchments checked for a Central Abbotsford address?

faq.a: The City Centre Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2913-2019) and Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2920-2019) are listed as adopted neighbourhood plans in the Abbotsford OCP framework, under the city-wide Abbotsforward 2050 Official Community Plan.
faq.q: Which plans govern the central area?

faq.a: City plan boards list Urban 1 – Midrise up to 6 storeys, Urban 2 – Ground Oriented for rowhouses, townhouse, multiplex or duplex housing, and Urban 3 – Infill for single detached dwellings with some ground-oriented duplexes.
faq.q: What housing forms does the Historic Downtown plan allow near the core?
